questions.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x+3z=-2 \\ x+y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
questions.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 & -2 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the standard method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 & -2 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now  

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x+3z=-2 \\ y-3z=2.\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=-2-3z \\ y=2+3z \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the latter can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2-3z \\ 2+3z \\ z\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Determine the value of $k$ for which the following system of linear equations is inconsistent:

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & x+4y=2 \\  & 2x+(k+1)y=3\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 2 \\ 2 & k+1 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 2 \\ 2 & k+1 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 2 \\ 0 & k-7 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x+4y=2 \\ (k-7)y=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

The system is inconsistent if it has no solutions. For the system to have no solutions, one of the equations above must be false.

If $k=7,$ then the second equation is $0=-1,$ which is false, and the system will have no solution.

Therefore, our system is inconsistent when $k=7.$

questions.problem:
Consider the following system of equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & x-4y=-1 \\  & 2x-7y=0 \\  & -4x+15y=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

I. The system is consistent independent

II. The system has no solution

III. The system is consistent dependent
questions.worked_solution:
To classify the system, we first need to find its solution. The augmented matrix for this system is 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 \\ 2 & -7 & 0 \\ -4 & 15 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 \\ 2 & -7 & 0 \\ -4 & 15 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ -4 & 15 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since any numbers $x$ and $y$ are solutions to the third equation $0x+0y=0$, we can remove this equation from the system. So, the corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x-4y=-1 \\ y=2.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation we have $y=2$ and substituting this into the first equation yields $x=7.$ So,  we conclude that the system is consistent independent. 

As a result, only statement I is true.

questions.problem:
Consider the following system of equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & 3x-3y=6 \\  & -2x+y=-3 \\  & 4x-4y=8.\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

I. The system is consistent dependent

II. The system is consistent independent

III. The system has no solution
questions.worked_solution:
To classify the system, we first need to find its solution. The augmented matrix for this system is 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & -3 & 6 \\ -2 & 1 & -3 \\ 4 & -4 & 8\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -3 & 6 \\ -2 & 1 & -3 \\ 4 & -4 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 & -3 \\ 4 & -4 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 \\ 4 & -4 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since any numbers $x$ and $y$ are solutions to the third equation $0x+0y=0$, we can remove this equation from the system. So, the corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x-y=2 \\ y=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation we have $y=-1$ and substituting this into the first equation yields $x=1.$ So,  we conclude that the system is consistent independent. 

As a result, only statement II is true.

questions.problem:
Determine the value of $k$ for which the following system of linear equations is inconsistent:

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & 2x-y=3 \\  & -4x+(k-5)y=-1\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 3 \\ -4 & k-5 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 3 \\ -4 & k-5 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & k-7 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x-y=3 \\ (k-7)y=5.\end{aligned}
$$

The system is inconsistent if it has no solutions. For the system to have no solutions, one of the equations above must be false.

If $k=7,$ then the second equation is $0=5,$ which is false, and the system will have no solution.

Therefore, our system is inconsistent when $k=7.$
